- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.4) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast increase to 2–3% for next 3 days to avoid overshoot.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (first 5–7 days of forecast) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast values.
- If sentiment shows strong divergence from price trend (e.g., sentiment rising while price falls), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction within 2–3 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for last 5–7 days if sentiment remains positive or volatile.
